key_insight: Raising the detonation-spray barrel filling ratio from 43% to 53% produced a denser Cr3C2–NiCr coating with better wear resistance, even though friction increased.
engineering_relevance: This suggests process-fill optimization can improve carbide coating durability for components exposed to severe sliding wear and high-load service.
method: Detonation-sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings were deposited at two barrel filling ratios: 43% and 53%.
Microstructure and phase composition were examined using microscopy and X-ray diffraction.
Tribology was tested by dry ball-on-disc sliding at 10 and 15 N and 5 and 10 cm/s.
evidence_signal: The 53% filling-ratio coating showed a denser microstructure and achieved a minimum wear rate of 1.23 × 10^-4 mm3/(m·N) under dry sliding tests.
watch_item: Higher filling ratio improved wear resistance, but the accompanying increase in friction means application-specific balancing of tribological tradeoffs is still needed.
paper_title: Effect of Barrel Filling Ratio on the Microstructure, Phase Composition and Tribological Performance of Detonation-Sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr Coatings
